To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
brain development continues actively during the second decade of life, as evidenced by longitudinal changes in both grey and white matter.

brain maturation during adolescence is associated with increases in the volume of white matter and in the fractional anisotrophy (an index of microstructure) of many fiber tracts in the brain, and with decreases in cortical grey matter.
brain maturation during adolescence involves increases in white matter volume and fractional anisaotropy, and decreases in grey matter volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the human brain during adolescence, a period of rapid change in the brain that has important implications for the development of the individual's personality, social and emotional skills, cognitive abilities and behaviour.
understanding the neural basis of adolescent behavior, and the role of the adolescent brain in psychopathology.
the development and application of novel imaging methods to investigate the structural and functional changes in the human brain that occur during adolescence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is maturing and developing in a highly specific way during adolescence.

brain maturation is associated with structural and anatomical changes enhancing long distance connectivity in different WM tractors, specifically in the arcuate fasciculus (AF) and corticospital tract (CST) while cortical grey matter exhibits synaptic "prunning".
the brain undergoes a complex process of maturation in adolescence, with increases in WM volume, FA values and axonal diameters, and reductions in GM volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adolescent brain is characterized by an increase in the volume of white matter, an increase in fractional anisotrophy, an increase in parallel diffusibility, a decrease in perpendicular diffusibility, and a decrease in grey matter volume.

the brain is not fully matured until at least the mid-twenties, and that the brain undergoes a series of complex changes during this period of life, including the development of long-distance connections and the "pruning" of cortical GM.
the brain is a dynamic organ that continues to change throughout adolescence and that these changes are reflected in the imaging data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not static during adolescence but rather is in a constant state of change.
there is a complex pattern of age related changes in the brain during adolescence, which may reflect the interplay of different processes such as synaptic pruning and myelination.
there is a clear need for more longitudinal studies of brain development in adolescence, and that DTI can provide useful data on age related changes in WM structure.
